content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Donna Ball (E024) requests write access to Payroll.

Notes:
- Note 1: role: Payroll Specialist, employment type: full_time, security training: basic
- Note 2: role: Payroll Specialist, employment type: contractor, security training: basic
- Note 3: role: Payroll Specialist, employment type: contractor, security training: basic, recommendation: read

There's conflicting information about employment type: one note says full_time, two say contractor. I should verify the employment type (or another field) using the verify tool. I can call verify at most once per ticket.

Let me think about what to verify. The conflict is between full_time and contractor. That determines the policy. Also role is consistent (Payroll Specialist). Training is basic in all notes.

If contractor: max is read (since basic training, no write). Requested write > max read, so grant read.
If full_time: max is write (up to write; admin only if role owns system - role is Payroll Specialist which owns Payroll, so admin is technically allowed). Full_time employee with role owning system: admin allowed. Requested write is at or below max (write ≤ admin), so grant write. Wait, actually max for full time is write, admin only if role owns system. Since Payroll Specialist owns Payroll, admin is possible. Requested write ≤ write maximum, so grant write.

So the decision hinges on employment type. Let me verify employment_type.

I'll call verify with employee_id E024, field employment_type.

Verified: employment type is contractor.

So the policy: contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Training is basic (all notes agree). So maximum access is read.

Requested: write. Write > read max, so grant maximum: read.

Submit decision: read.
